title: Trumpeter and arranger Joe Phillips
summary: Albert mentions Jack Willis and the Keyhole, then praises Joe Phillips, a trumpeter and arranger from his band who never talked much.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Telephone. No, it's not Jack Willis.

I'll tell you when Jack came in. Jack didn't work in my band. Mm-hmm. But Jack did come to San Antonio when I'd given up the band with Freddie Coleman's little band at the first keyhole nightclub that I had. Mm-hmm. But there was a fellow yesterday at the concert that they very seldom mentioned around here. I thought was a great trumpet player. He played in my band. Joe Phillips. Yes.
Did you see Joe? I did. And he...
Now, he's another guy that did some arranging.

Yes. We talked about that. I talked to him on the phone, but he didn't recognize me on the phone. Excuse me. So he said he could tell me a lot more about it. You know when you call people up sometimes and they don't know you.

Well, people have a tendency today to ignore everybody. And fortunately, I'm not one of those. I love to talk and I love to find out who the person is that I'm talking to. Oh. But Joe Phillips never was a talker.
